subject: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@finbot.ai>, Elena Gomez <elena@finbot.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps

Hi Samir / Elena,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Below is a short recap to make sure we captured the key pain points, success criteria, and next steps. Please flag anything we missed.

Pain points you described:
- Unit economics are the primary constraint: inference spend has grown ~3x in the last 6 months and is eating into margins.
- High tail latency and occasional cold-starts affecting real-time flows (customer support and fraud scoring).
- Current batching is manual and inconsistent across services; prefix caching is limited.
- Openness to quantization but worried about quality regressions for your NLU models.

Current stack (what you told us):
- Self-hosted endpoints on AWS (g4dn / g5-like instances) running Hugging Face/Open weights via a homegrown autoscaler.
- Fronting services in k8s; async workers handle batch requests.
- Average request: 350 tokens input, 60 tokens output; peak concurrency ~120 rps.

Success criteria (what a win looks like):
- Reduce inference cost per 1k requests by ~3x without degrading P95 latency beyond 150ms for customer-facing endpoints.
- Maintain or improve model output quality (no measurable drop on your eval set).
- Easy integration with existing k8s and SSO for Private deployment if we go that route.

Where Redwood can help (initial hypotheses):
- Continuous batching + prefix/KV caching to drop per-token cost and raise GPU utilization.
- Quantization evaluation (4-bit/INT8) with A/B quality checks on your eval prompts.
- Model routing: cheaper model variants for non-critical traffic and fallbacks for capacity events.

Open items / what we need from you:
- Sample traffic statistics and a small eval prompt set (we referenced finbot_mvp_usage_stats.csv) — ideally anonymized.
- Confirmation if you have any regulatory constraints that require on-prem / VPC deployment.

Next steps:
1) You share the usage CSV + eval prompts (Samir) — target: end of week.
2) Aditya/Marissa to schedule a 45-min pilot scoping call with Infra + ML Eng (proposed: Mon 11/23).
3) We’ll provide an initial perf/cost hypothesis and a pilot plan (3–4 weeks) prior to any costs.

Attachments: finbot_mvp_usage_stats.csv (sample usage), demo screens reference video (redwood-demo-screens.mov).

Thanks — looking forward to the pilot.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

Thanks Aditya — this looks right. A couple quick clarifications:
- The 3x increase is month-over-month on token spend for the transaction classification models; overall company spend is up ~2.5x.
- We can share a redacted eval set (10k prompts) but need to remove any PII first — Elena will coordinate.
- For deployment, we prefer VPC-first but are open to a hosted pilot if the data never leaves our account.

I’ll get the CSV + eval set to you by Friday EOD. Quick ask: can Marissa join the scoping call on Monday? She owns infra prioritization.

Samir
VP of Engineering | FinBot
samir.patel@finbot.ai | +1 650 555 9821

Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 08:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps

Appreciate the quick turnaround Samir. Yes — Marissa will join the scoping call. A few more details to set expectations before the pilot: 
- Pilot scope (3 weeks): verify batching/caching savings on a representative workload, run quantization experiments (4-bit and int8) on a subset of your models, and validate latency SLOs at p95.
- Deliverables: cost delta report, quality regression analysis (your eval set vs quantized runs), and deployment options (hosted vs private VPC).
- We’ll need a staging endpoint or sample traffic replay (you can point us to a signed URL or share via secure Drive).

Proposed times for the scoping call (PT): Mon 11/23 9:00am, 11:00am, or 2:00pm — which works best?

I’ll attach the pilot checklist after you confirm.

Best,
Aditya

From: Elena Gomez <elena@finbot.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@finbot.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps

Thanks — Monday 11/23 11:00am PT works for us.

Action items I’ll own:
- Redact and share the eval prompts + the finbot_mvp_usage_stats.csv by Friday (uploading to the Drive link Aditya listed).
- Provide a short doc on regulatory constraints (we’re PCI-adjacent; no PHI).
- Point you to a staging replay URL with auth for the pilot team.

We’re open to trying 4-bit quantization on the non-customer-facing path first; we want to see quality numbers before wider rollout. Also, batching is a high priority — anything that reduces per-request cpu/gpu time will help our cost goals.

See you Mon 11/23 at 11:00am PT.
